coverage.diagram_math_review: The theorem's statement, facts and proof render legibly in both original-resolution tiles. No existing diagram or diagram error is present. A schematic can be useful for distinguishing closure, same-group conjugation, and stabilization/destabilization, provided it follows the exact move conventions recorded in the candidate checks.

candidates.source_claim: The theorem identifies equivalence of oriented closures with finite sequences of conjugations in one B_n and positive or negative stabilizations β↦ι_n(β)σ_n^{±1} into B_{n+1}, together with inverse destabilizations. Its proof uses closure preservation for each move and a factorization result for closed braid diagrams.
candidates.diagram_kind: schematic closure and Markov move comparison
candidates.why_warranted: A compact schematic can make the theorem's two levels visible: a braid closes to an oriented link, while braid representatives of an isotopic closure may differ by same-strand conjugation or a one-strand Markov stabilization/destabilization. This is useful context for a central theorem, though the prose statement and proof are already legible and complete without a diagram.
concrete_content_to_draw_or_check: Show a generic n-strand braid β as a box and its oriented closure β̂ as the link obtained by the stated closure construction; avoid assigning a specific crossing word to β.
Show conjugation β↦γβγ⁻¹ as a move B_n→B_n, with strand count n on both sides; any closure comparison should be schematic and should not claim that γβγ⁻¹ is braid-isotopic to β.
Show positive and negative stabilization β↦ι_n(β)σ_n^{±1} as B_n→B_{n+1}; the new strand is on the right, and the new generator is σ_n with exponent sign ±.
Show destabilization in the inverse direction B_{n+1}→B_n only as the inverse Markov move, reducing the strand count by one.

If showing a geometric product decomposition, retain the fixed target-basepoint inclusion ι_n(β)·σ_n^{±1} and the stated rightmost-factor-traversed-first convention; do not move the new generator into an arbitrary position in the word.
Indicate that closure isotopy is the equivalence relation concluded by the theorem and that the diagram illustrates the move types rather than proving the factorization assertion.
correctness_checks: Conjugation is γβγ⁻¹ and stays inside the same B_n; it does not change strand count.
Stabilization uses the standard inclusion ι_n:B_n→B_{n+1}, adds the new strand on the right, and multiplies by the target generator σ_n^{±1}; both signs occur.
Destabilization is an inverse move from B_{n+1} to B_n. Do not imply that an arbitrary braid has an inverse destabilization or that stabilization is available from B_0, where σ_0 does not exist.
The convention states that the rightmost product factor is traversed first in geometric time. A word-level picture must respect this order and the fixed product position.
The added strand is expressed at the first n target basepoints; the source explicitly warns that the old parametrized strands are not literally left untouched because the target basepoints differ.
Distinguish braid isotopy of representatives from Markov moves between braid groups and from ambient isotopy/equivalence of their oriented closures.
candidates.why_not_confirmed: No diagram or mathematical defect was observed. The proposed illustration is optional teaching support, and the screenshot shows no rendering failure; absence of art alone does not establish a defect.

frozen_source_lines.text: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\beta,\beta'$ be braids. Then
$\widehat\beta$ and $\widehat{\beta'}$ are equivalent oriented links if and
only if $\beta$ and $\beta'$ are Markov equivalent, that is, related by a finite
sequence of conjugations in a fixed braid group, stabilizations
$\beta\mapsto\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ into the next braid group, and their

Use the closed braid diagrams obtained from the closure construction applied to $\beta$ and $\beta'$, and read each diagram at its original cutting ray. The braids read this way are $\beta$ and $\beta'$ themselves, up to braid isotopy. Apply [F3] to these two diagrams to obtain their Markov equivalence. If a different cutting ray is used, [F2] gives a conjugate braid, which lies in the same Markov class.

bound_move_definition_checks: Conjugation is γβγ⁻¹ in B_n and leaves the strand count unchanged.
For n≥1, stabilization is ι_n(β)·σ_n or ι_n(β)·σ_n⁻¹ in B_{n+1}; the new strand is on the right.
The product convention traverses the rightmost factor first; the fixed stabilization product position should be retained.
At n=0 there is no σ_0, so the empty braid has no stabilization move.
